r3-evidence.title: Required evidence
r3-evidence.imperative: Is the required evidence present and does it actually demonstrate the behavior? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r3-evidence.finding: Reproduced BOTH load-bearing evidences myself, not trusted from the report: (1) pytest tests/unit/physics/instrument_panel/test_variance_decomposition.py -q -> 7 passed in 0.49s (matches implementer claim exactly). (2) pyright on variance_decomposition.py -> 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 informations (matches claim). Independently wrote a scratch script (outside repo, read-only) reusing the SAME generative model against fit_two_way directly: correct mapping reproduces pure_car -> car_reference=0.999/driver_utilization=0.000 and pure_driver -> car_reference=0.000/driver_utilization=0.997 (matches test thresholds <0.1). Then SWAPPED the mapping (car_reference<-frac_team, driver_utilization<-frac_circuit) on the identical synthetic data: pure_car swapped driver_utilization=0.999 (test asserts <0.1 -> would FAIL), pure_driver swapped car_reference=0.997 (test asserts <0.1 -> would FAIL). Confirms the two per-share falsification tests genuinely depend on the correct mapping and would fail if swapped -- not tautological. Also confirmed a hardcoded constant share (e.g. driver_utilization always 0.33 across the b-sweep) fails the monotonic-rise assertion (shares[-1] > shares[0]+0.1) -- hardcoding is caught too. Confirmatory sum/bounds evidence (shares in [0,1] summing to ~1.0 via _assert_valid_shares) is exercised on every one of the 7 tests, not just one spot example.

r4-quality.title: Quality vs inherited rules
r4-quality.imperative: Does the change meet the inherited project/section rules (the handoff's constraints)? Append a check per rule. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r4-quality.finding: Constraint checks: (1) Pure/deterministic -- confirmed, no I/O, no RNG in production code, numpy-only arithmetic delegated to fit_two_way. (2) Additive-pool-only / no interaction term -- confirmed by reading pooling.py's fit_two_way (y=mu+team_effect+circuit_effect+residual, no cross term) and variance_decomposition.py (5-line pass-through, adds nothing). (3) Driver-utilization=floor -- driver_utilization_is_floor is a hardcoded True field, always set, matches constraint:no-frame-kill. (4) F12-independent -- no DB import, no REPLICATION_* reference anywhere in the new files (grep-confirmed by reading full file contents). (5) Structure/state rules (CREW_CONTEXT) -- no module-level mutable state, no DatabaseManager, no impure caching. (6) simplification_limits -- reproduced myself: 'PASS (4 files checked)' on src/physics/instrument_panel + tests/unit/physics/instrument_panel. (7) Physics truth-anchoring (L1-L4) -- the synthetic-recovery tests use a BALANCED grid (n_reps=8 per driver x class cell), for which fit_two_way's method-of-moments is exact per its own docstring, so recovery-to-known-coefficient is L1/L2-level truth anchoring, satisfying 'new physics models need truth-anchored tests.' (8) Region verification -- handoff scoped required evidence to the narrow test file; I additionally ran the reused seam's own suite (tests/unit/physics/layer2/test_pooling.py, 15 tests) together with the new instrument_panel tests: 22 passed in 0.56s, confirming the read-only reuse didn't disturb pooling.py's own contract.
